speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your sudden vertigo, could you describe exactly what the spinning sensation feels like and how long each episode lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Do you experience any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the vertigo start or worsen when you changed your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, do you have any history of recent head trauma or ear infections?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the spinning sensation return if you roll over in bed or look up right now? I also need to know if you have any hearing loss or ringing in your ears.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying those symptoms. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to perform a physical exam maneuver; please lie down and turn your head 45 degrees to the right, then quickly lie back while keeping your head turned, and tell me if the spinning sensation returns.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
